points.gloss: marks what you eat, read, buy…

connect.pos: Noun (the thing you eat, read, buy…)
connect.rule: 〜{を}[食|た]べます／〜{を}[読|よ]みます／〜{を}[買|か]います

examples.ja: [毎日|まいにち]パン{を}[食|た]べます。
きのう、この[本|ほん]{を}[読|よ]みました。

watch.note: The thing you eat, drink, read or buy takes を, not が. が is for the thing that is there, as in 水があります.
watch.bad: 毎日コーヒーが飲みます。
watch.good: 毎日コーヒーを飲みます。

connect.pos: Place you go to (へ is read え)
connect.rule: 〜{へ}[行|い]きます／[来|き]ます／かえります

connect.pos: Place you go to (same meaning with に)
connect.rule: 〜{に}[行|い]きます／[来|き]ます／かえります

examples.ja: あした、[大学|だいがく]{へ}[行|い]きます。
examples.en: I am going to the university tomorrow.

examples.ja: [先週|せんしゅう]、[友|とも]だちが[日本|にほん]{に}[来|き]ました。
examples.en: My friend came to Japan last week.

watch.note: The place you are going to takes へ or に, not を. へ is said え, but it is always written へ.
watch.bad: あした、学校を行きます。
watch.good: あした、学校へ行きます。

compare.intro: All three come after a noun. The verb after it tells you which one you need.

forms.tag: なにを？ · what you buy, eat, read

forms.en: I go to the flower shop.

forms.ja: [駅|えき]に[花|はな]や{が}あります。
forms.en: There is a flower shop at the station.

check.label: ともだちと
check.q: あした、[友|とも]だちのうち（　　）[行|い]きます。
why: を marks the thing you eat, read or buy. The house is the place you go to.
The friend's house is where you go, and the place before 行きます takes へ.
うちが行きます would make the house the one who goes.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [父|ちち]は[毎日|まいにち][新聞|しんぶん]（　　）^[読|よ]みます^。
why: The newspaper is the thing he reads, so it takes を.
へ marks the place you go to. 読みます is not going anywhere.
With 読みます, the thing you read takes を, not が. 父は already says who reads.
に here would mark a place you go to. A newspaper is not a place.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: らいしゅう、[日本|にほん]（　　）^[行|い]きます^。
why: Japan is where you are going, and the place before 行きます takes へ.
を does not mark the place you go to.
日本が行きます would make Japan the one who goes.
で marks where you do something, not where you go.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: A：きのう[何|なに]（　　）[買|か]いましたか。　B：^[本|ほん]を^[買|か]いました。
why: A asks about the thing B bought, so 何 takes を, just like 本を in B's answer.
へ marks the place you go to. 買いました is not going anywhere.
The thing you buy takes を, not が.
何は does not work in this question. The thing you buy takes を.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [先週|せんしゅう]、[母|はは]がわたしのうち^に^（　　）。
why: うちに is the place she came to, so the verb is one of coming: 来ました.
My house is not something you eat, and うちに needs a verb of going or coming.
My house is not something you read, and うちに needs a verb of going or coming.
うちに with 買いました does not make sense here. うちに needs a verb of going or coming.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: 新しい goes right before the thing it describes. Which tile marks the thing you read?
drill.full: わたしはきのう[新|あたら]しい[本|ほん]{を}[読|よ]みました。
drill.explain: 新しい goes right before 本. The thing you read takes を, and the verb comes last: わたしはきのう新しい本を読みました, "I read a new book yesterday."

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: Where are you going? Which tile marks that place?
drill.full: あした、[母|はは]と[新|あたら]しいデパート{へ}[行|い]きます。
drill.explain: 新しい goes right before デパート. The place you go to takes へ, and 行きます comes last: あした、母と新しいデパートへ行きます, "Tomorrow I am going to the new department store with my mother."

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: A：きのう　何を　しましたか。　B：ともだちと　えいが（　　）　見ました。
exam.explain: The film is the thing they watched, so it takes を. へ and に mark a place you go to, and with 見ました the thing you watch does not take が.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.explain: くにへ marks the place you go to, so the verb must be one of moving: かえります, "I will go back to my country." 食べます and 読みます take a thing with を, and あります takes a place with に, not へ.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: 父は　きのう　大きい　魚{を}　買いました。
exam.explain: 大きい, 魚, を, 買いました. 大きい goes right before 魚, the thing he bought takes を, and the verb comes last.

scene.intro: Tap every word you would read on the platform signs and the departure board.

words.gloss: University (station name: in front of the university)

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: あ、_でんしゃ_が　来ましたよ。
check.explain: でんしゃ, "train", is written 電車: 電 (electricity) and 車 (vehicle). 雨 (rain) is only the top part of 電, and 東 (east) looks like 車 but is a different kanji. 雨車, 電東 and 雨東 are not words.

item.q: 男の人は　はじめに　何を　買いますか。
script: ナレーター：駅で、女の人と男の人が話しています。男の人は、はじめに、何を買いますか。
女：電車は十時半ですね。まだ二十分ありますよ。
男：じゃあ、ぼく、店へ行きます。パンとおちゃを買います。
女：パンはありますよ。わたしのかばんの中です。
男：そうですか。じゃあ、おちゃを買います。
女：あ、でも、きっぷは買いましたか。
女：じゃあ、きっぷが先ですよ。
男：そうですね。おちゃは、あとで買います。
ナレーター：男の人は、はじめに、何を買いますか。
why: This was his first plan, but the woman already has bread in her bag.
The woman says パンはありますよ: the bread is in her bag, so he does not buy it.
He has not bought a ticket yet (まだです), and the woman says きっぷが先ですよ, "the ticket comes first".
He will buy tea, but he says おちゃは、あとで買います: later, after the ticket.
